alignments.note: Rule 14: the waw of the consecutive form takes whatever connective the ASV writes for it; here the ASV writes no 'And' but 'came again', and 'again' stands where the connective would stand (cf. v.20 'And', v.11 'Moreover' for the identical Hebrew). Competing reading: 'again' is an adverb inside the verb's rendering and the waw is unrepresented; I took the connective reading because the ASV's word does the connective work in this formula.
The verb takes the verb (rule 14); no presentative frame is written here.
Construct noun; no article morpheme is present in the chain, so the ASV's 'The' is supplied on the construct under rule 29.
Nomen rectum takes the relational 'of' (rule 19), headed on the name.
Pronominal suffix takes the object pronoun (rule 18).
The lamed of לֵאמֹר has no English realization (rule 27).

review_notes: The one judgment call is the waw: aligned to 'again' rather than left unrepresented, with the competing reading recorded in that unit's note.
